standard: NFPA 13 (2019 edition) - Table 27.2.3.1.1, Equivalent Schedule 40 Steel Pipe Length Chart
note: Equivalent length in FEET of Schedule 40 steel pipe, keyed by the same nominalSize strings as reference/pipes/*.json. A size missing from a fitting's map is not published for that fitting (shown as a dash in the table) -- SprinklerHydraulicCalculator throws for that combination rather than assuming zero, and a caller can pass an explicit equivalentLengthFt instead. 10 in. and 12 in. are transcribed for completeness even though reference/pipes/*.json currently stops at 8 in.
cFactorBasisNote: Published lengths are in feet of C=120 pipe. SprinklerHydraulicCalculator rescales them for the segment's own C by (C/120)^1.85, which reproduces NFPA's published multipliers (0.713 at C=100, 1.16 at C=130, 1.33 at C=140, 1.51 at C=150). Note the direction: rougher pipe (lower C) needs FEWER equivalent feet, so dry/preaction steel at C=100 gets shorter lengths than printed here. The inverse form (120/C)^1.85 does not match the published factors. An explicitly supplied equivalentLengthFt on a fitting is never rescaled, since the caller's basis is unknown.
transcriptionNote: SECOND READ DONE for every row. The transcription was checked cell-for-cell against the printed 2019 Table 27.2.3.1.1 (all eight rows, fifteen sizes, the dashes included), and earlier against two independent reproductions of the same chart (a 2016-edition copy, where this table is numbered 23.4.3.1.1, and a commercial sprinkler design program's NFPA table). Two oddities are published, not transcription slips: the butterfly valve really is 12 ft at 4 in. and 9 ft at 5 in. (identical in both editions and in the program's table), and swing check values are averages per the table's own footnote because equivalent length varies with valve design. 1/2 in. appears only because NFPA 13 allows that size in existing-system modifications (Sections 29.4 and 29.5).
vaneFlowSwitchResolution: VANE_TYPE_FLOW_SWITCH is in the printed 2019 Table 27.2.3.1.1 and every value agrees: 1 in. 6, 1-1/4 in. 9, 1-1/2 in. 10, 2 in. 14, 2-1/2 in. 17, 3 in. 22, 4 in. 30, 6 in. 16, 8 in. 22, 10 in. 29, 12 in. 36, with 1/2, 3/4, 3-1/2 and 5 in. not published. The earlier doubt came from the two reproductions used as second readers, neither of which carries the row; the printed 2019 table does, so the row stays and is tagged 'verified'.
